quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Electric TDnet: Mitsubishi Electric to Form Joint Venture with ABB for (10-20-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Mitsubishi Electric entered into a joint venture agreement (definitive agreement executed October 20, 2026) with ABB Corporation, the Japanese subsidiary of ABB, for its low-voltage power distribution business: low-voltage circuit breakers, electromagnetic switches, measurement and control equipment and UPS for general industrial use of 5kVA or less, plus sales of certain high-voltage power distribution control equipment, related service functions and the development and manufacturing of smart meters. A new wholly owned company (establishment planned December 1, 2026) succeeds to the business by an absorption-type company split (split agreement planned August 1, 2027; effective October 1, 2027), and 51% of its shares are then transferred to ABB Corporation (closing planned October 1, 2027, subject to approvals from competition-law and other authorities in Japan and overseas and contractual preconditions). The new company then becomes a joint venture owned 51% by ABB Corporation and 49% by Mitsubishi Electric - a consolidated subsidiary of ABB and an equity-method affiliate of Mitsubishi Electric, with a seven-member board (five directors nominated by ABB, two by Mitsubishi Electric). Related sales operations of overseas sales subsidiaries are expected to move to ABB's local entities. The business to be split (within the Industry & Mobility segment) had net sales of 102.2 billion yen in the fiscal year ended March 2026 (internal management figures, unaudited). The consolidated forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 announced July 31, 2026 does not include the impact of the transactions. Senior Executive Officer and Group President, Factory Automation Systems, Takayuki Tsuzuki: through the joint venture the company will combine ABB's global business foundation with its own technologies, quality, customer base and sales channels, aiming to provide higher value to customers and further grow its power distribution product business.
